headlines.title: Giants trade left-handed starting pitcher Robbie Ray to Padres for two prospects
headlines.description: The Giants parted with one of their two ace-caliber starting pitchers. San Francisco traded left-handed pitcher Robbie Ray to the San Diego Padres on Monday, the team announced after ESPN’s Jeff Passan first reported the news. The Giants received right-handed pitching prospect Miguel Mendez and shortstop prospect Joniel Hernandez from San Diego. The 24-year-old Mendez was the Padres’ No. 4 prospect, according to MLB.com, and in 12 combined starts across the High-A and Double-A levels this season, posted a 4.79 ERA with 39 strikeouts and 17 walks in 35 2/3 innings pitched. Hernandez, 17, was San Diego’s No. 9 prospect, and batted .303/.424/.503 with four home runs and 43 RBI in 155 at-bats in rookie ball. Since his June 16 outing, Ray has been one of MLB’s best starters, posting a 1.65 ERA and 61 strikeouts in 60 innings. In his final Giants start against the San Diego Padres on Thursday at Petco Park, Ray allowed four hits and one earned run while striking out six in six dominant innings. “I tried to put everything out of my head leading up to this start, but yeah, it obviously comes up now that this could be my last start in a Giants uniform,” Ray said following Thursday’s outing. San Francisco originally acquired Ray in a trade with the Seattle Mariners in Jan. 2024 as the former Cy Young Award winner was rehabbing from Tommy John surgery. Ray eventually debuted with the Giants on July 24 of that year, making seven starts before the season ended. A fully healthy Ray then returned to Cy Young form in the first half of the 2025 MLB season, earning his second All-Star nod, before trailing off toward the end of the campaign. In 61 appearances (60 starts) across three seasons with San Francisco, Ray posted a combined 3.54 ERA with 336 strikeouts and 145 walks across 335 2/3 innings pitched. He now will join righty Michael King atop the the Padres’ starting rotation, while two intriguing prospects join a rising Giants farm system. Download and follow the Giants Talk Podcast

headlines.title: Giants trade Luis Arraez, Caleb Kilian to Phillies for two pitching prospects
headlines.description: The Giants made a difficult, yet expected move. San Francisco traded All-Star second baseman Luis Arraez and relief pitcher Caleb Kilian to the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday, the team announced after ESPN’s Jeff Passan and The Athletic’s Jayson Stark first reported the news. The Giants received pitching prospects Ramon Marquez and Marty Gair in the deal with the Phillies. San Francisco signed Arraez to a one-year, $12 million free-agent contract last offseason. Despite initial concerns regarding the veteran second baseman’s defense, Arraez quickly proved to be a more than serviceable defender at the position after working with Giants infield coach Ron Washington. However, his biggest impact throughout the first half of the 2026 MLB season was with the bat. In 105 games with San Francisco before the trade, Arraez batted .324/.360/.440 with four home runs, 43 RBI and 10 stolen bases, earning him his fourth career All-Star nod. With Arraez on the move and Casey Schmitt on the injured list with a torn left meniscus, the Giants likely will use Christian Koss and Osleivis Basabe at second base. San Francisco might not be done making moves, either. Download and follow the Giants Talk Podcast

headlines.title: San Francisco Firebells pick up first win of the season
headlines.description: San Francisco’s women’s professional baseball team made history Sunday after winning its first game of the season. The Firebells opened their inaugural season with a 11-3 victory over the Boston Hunters. The win came one day after the league’s first ever game with the Los Angeles Queens versus the New York Heights. Kelsie Whitmore, the No. 1 overall pick, helped lead the way in the franchise’s debut. “I know this is just game one. We have a long season ahead. The goal is to keep the energy that we have, the momentum. Love the squad that we’re on, just keep it going,” Whitmore said. The Firebells will face off against the Heights on Thursday and the Queens on Friday.

headlines.title: 5 men arrested by Walnut Creek police in online child sex crime sting
headlines.description: Four men from across the Bay Area and one visiting from Europe were arrested by Walnut Creek police this week for allegedly traveling to the city to meet up with children for sexual exploitation. The Walnut Creek Police Department in conjunction with the Contra Costa County Crimes Against Children Task Force targeted adults using social media to target children. According to police, five men are now facing allegations of attempted lewd acts with a minor, contacting a minor to commit a sex offense, and arranging to meet a minor for sex. Arrested were Concord resident Andrew Garcia, 32, Antioch resident Billie Ray Breland, 29, and Taesu Park, 36, from Marin County. A man visiting from Germany was also arrested, Rudolf Naused Robl, 42, and a Walnut Creek resident, Jacek Markiewicz, 76, was also arrested on suspicion of attempted kidnapping.

headlines.title: Bystanders resuscitate teen at San Mateo County beach
headlines.description: Good Samaritans resuscitated a teenager who appeared to have drowned at San Gregorio State Beach in San Mateo County on Sunday, according to Cal Fire. First responders were called to the beach south of Half Moon Bay on a report of an 18-year-old found unconscious in the lagoon area, Cal Fire said. Authorities believe the person had been submerged in water for a minimum of two minutes and was found unresponsive and not breathing. “Thanks to the immediate action of quick-thinking bystanders who called 911 and started early Bystander CPR, the patient regained breathing and consciousness prior to the arrival of first responders,” Cal Fire said. Multiple agencies arrived at the scene and the patient was transported to the hospital, where they were reported in stable condition. headlines.title: Oakland teen charged in alleged beating of 15-year-old
headlines.description: An Oakland teen was charged in the assault and robbery of a juvenile, the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office said Friday. Jaeden Roach, 18, was charged with allegedly assaulting a 15-year-old juvenile with a firearm, robbery, and felony child endangerment, prosecutors said. According to the District Attorney’s Office, on June 25 at about 3:15 p.m., Roach was allegedly one of five suspects who hid themselves behind an apartment complex in the 3400 block of 68th Avenue in Oakland. The group allegedly waited for the 15-year-old to arrive, and then the juvenile was attacked and beaten with handguns, causing serious injuries. Roach is scheduled to be arraigned Monday in Oakland.

headlines.title: 4 firefighters injured in six-alarm fire at Foster City condominium complex
headlines.description: Crews remained at the scene Monday checking for hot spots after a massive fire tore through a Foster City condominium complex Sunday afternoon. Four firefighters suffered minor injuries while battling the six-alarm blaze at the Spinnaker Cove condominium complex at 815 Sea Spray Lane, according to Foster City police. Police said two firefighters were taken to the hospital — one for second-degree burns on the back and shoulders and the other for smoke inhalation. Two additional firefighters were treated at the scene and continued working. The fire broke out shortly after 2:30 p.m. Sunday on the first floor before spreading through the building and reaching the third floor. Firefighters said windy conditions and hot weather fueled the flames, prompting a response from departments across the Peninsula. Residents trapped inside were rescued, including some from third-floor windows, while others evacuated safely with their pets as thick smoke rose above the complex. “Rescue was a priority, as a number of people were calling and saying that they were trapped,” San Mateo Consolidated Fire Chief Matt Turturici said. “There were numerous people taken down from the third floor … and there were numerous rescues down the stairwells.” No residents were injured. During the response, one firefighter issued a mayday after becoming separated from a partner inside the building. The two firefighters were later safely reunited. Police advised nearby residents to avoid the area and close their windows because of heavy smoke. Road closures were also expected nearby. Investigators are expected to examine what caused the fire now that crews have largely knocked down the flames. Families displaced by the fire are being directed to the clubhouse at the complex, where the American Red Cross is providing emergency assistance, shelter information and other resources.

headlines.title: Overnight Hwy. 101 closures begin between South San Francisco and East Palo Alto
headlines.description: Overnight lane and ramp closures will begin along U.S. Highway 101 on Monday between South San Francisco and East Palo Alto as Caltrans crews carry out road work. The intermittent closures are scheduled from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. on weeknights through Aug. 31. Crews will perform paving, guardrail installation and electrical work during the overnight hours, Caltrans said. Motorists should expect delays, allow extra travel time and use caution when traveling in the area.

headlines.title: San Ramon Valley to play for spot in Little League World Series
headlines.description: Danville-based San Ramon Valley Little League on Thursday night won the Northern California regional tournament, the third of four tournaments a Bay Area youth baseball team must win to make it to the Little League World Series. San Ramon Valley defeated a team from El Dorado Hills 12-2 in Chico on Thursday to win the NorCal tournament for children up to 12 years old. The team earlier won its Little League district championship, then last week won their section tournament in Castro Valley before winning the NorCal one. Next up will be the West Region tournament in San Bernardino starting Aug. 9 as one of four teams vying to make it to the Little League World Series in Williamsport, Pennsylvania. The international tournament brings together some of the best youth baseball teams from countries around the world. San Ramon Valley Little League posted on social media that it is the first time since 1993 that a 12U team from their league won the NorCal title. Two other Bay Area teams from Mill Valley and Los Gatos also made it to this year’s NorCal tournament. While the dream of every Little Leaguer is to make it to Williamsport on the East Coast, Little League’s Intermediate 50/70 World Series for the next age bracket of up to 13 year olds takes place annually a little closer to home in Livermore. Two Bay Area teams will compete in this year’s tournament, Bollinger Canyon from San Ramon, which won its district championship to earn the host team berth, and Granada from Livermore, which defeated a Moorpark team from Southern California in the West Region championship in Arizona on Thursday. The two will be among six teams from the U.S. and six international teams competing in the tournament at Max Baer Park in Livermore starting Sunday.

headlines.title: Last day to weigh in on new name for San Jose's downtown plaza
headlines.description: Monday is the last day for the public to weigh in on a new name for San Jose’s downtown plaza formerly known as Plaza de César Chávez. On Sunday, families flocked downtown so their kids could cool off in the fountains. And while many here still refer to this spot as Plaza de Cesar Chavez, after more than three decades that’s no longer the official name. The city launched a renaming process in June following explosive sexual abuse allegations against Chavez. After receiving more than 600 suggestions, the city has narrowed down the new names to these five and is asking residents to vote. The options are: Farmworkers Plaza Plaza de Quetzalcoatl Plaza de San Jose Plaza de Pueblo Plaza Park. Carlos Valencia of San Jose has already picked his favorite. “I would choose Plaza de San Jose. It’s a simple name. It represents San Jose culture, and you really don’t wanna complicate things by selecting a name that you can’t pronounce. Plaza de San Jose is the perfect match name for the plaza,” he said. Carmen Guerra also likes the name plaza de San Jose. “Because that’s the name of the city and it’s also in front of San Jose State University and I think the information will be more easy for tourist who visit San Jose,” she said. Some residents asked why it wasn’t an option to name the 2-acre park after labor icon Dolores Huerta. That’s because the city’s naming policy requires a proposed name to meet specific criteria such as representing a geographic location, a historical event or an individual who typically must’ve been deceased for at least five years. Residents are asked to go to the city’s website and rank their choices by midnight Monday in a survey. The results will be presented to the parks and recreation commission on Sept. 2 and the commission will forward its recommendation to the city council, which will make the final decision on the park’s new name.

headlines.title: Neighbors frustrated after illegal sideshow involving over 100 cars in Vallejo
headlines.description: Police received multiple calls reporting a sideshow involving more than 100 cars and spectators, some throwing fireworks, early Sunday morning in Vallejo. After 2 a.m. Sunday, a large group of cars and people came out on Georgia Street and Columbus Parkway. Police say as officers converged on the group several people threw fireworks at responding patrol units. That was after police received calls about a sideshow with more than 100 cars. Police say by 3 a.m. in the morning, the groups in the sideshow left the city. Vallejo police say they have seen a significant reduction in sideshow activity this year compared to prior years. They attribute that to a coordinated response with allied agencies – as they had overnight – and proactive enforcement efforts. They say there have been about six recorded sideshows in 2026. Marta lives in the area and says it was frustrating. “People with phone and everything, going in circles and the smell, loud, it sounds like they’re doing fireworks or something, but it was very scary, I have two pets which they got very very scared, it’s awful,” she said. Other neighbors also said that, when this happens, they can’t rest. “They have fireworks. You see how hot it is? We got bushes, there is no houses behind me, they can spark a fire,” Carolyn said. Police say they understand the frustrations illegal sideshows cause. “These events create significant safety risks for the participants the spectators our residents and the motorists who are not involved, the Vallejo Police Department remains committed to addressing side shows,” they said.

headlines.title: 3 displaced after home fire in Fremont
headlines.description: Three people were displaced following a home fire in Fremont on Sunday afternoon, according to the fire department. Fire officials said at around 5:13 p.m. they received multiple calls regarding a house fire at 40174 Spady Street in the Irvington area of Fremont. The fire department said firefighters were able to contain the blaze, but since the house had a double roof, they had to cut up the home. Authorities said the house was declared a total loss, and three people were displaced. The fire department added nobody was hurt.
